observed_problem: Core v2 has profile constructors, initialization commands, settled stage handlers and production workflows, but W33/SP001 launch inputs and the start/resume decision procedure are not represented by one durable Core v2 bootstrap authority. The only concrete W33/SP001 values live in an in-memory regression fixture, while docs/special-session-bootstrap.md governs the legacy Special pipeline rather than Core v2.
expected_behavior: A fresh session must be able to resolve W33 or SP001 from repository state alone, dry-run the exact Profile that would be initialized, distinguish unstarted/resumable/partial-invalid state, initialize only when authorized after the coherent candidate is merged to main, and then resume through the canonical one-stage handoff/adoption path without reconstructing launch scope from chat history.
actual_behavior: A continuation agent can discover low-level CLIs but must infer which W33/SP001 inputs are canonical, when SP001 as_of is fixed, which work branch/path identities are expected, and how an existing or partially initialized Pilot is resumed. That leaves Pilot startup operationally chat-dependent despite green component tests.
production_workaround: External W33/SP001 production remains blocked until the coherent Core v2 candidate is Human-reviewed and merged; the Pilot registry, fail-closed planner/initializer and Core v2 session bootstrap runbook are now repository-owned and regression-covered.
improvement_action: Add a machine-readable W33/SP001 Pilot bootstrap registry, a fail-closed bootstrap planner/initializer that materializes SET_AT_INITIALIZATION time explicitly and never starts production during dry-run, a Core v2 session bootstrap runbook with start/resume/Human Gate/Exception Gate rules, and regression coverage proving both Pilot identities can be reconstructed without creating Production State.
